# Practitioners: Pierre Herubel and the round 2 experts

Research round 2, 2026-10-30. Three sources were read: 23 newsletters from
Pierre Herubel and outreach vendors, Herubel's public
pages and interviews, and 17 recognised experts or datasets the pack covered thinly. Every claim is in
`evidence.md` with its strength; every link, sender and date is in `sources.md`. The tests and the decisions are
in `../method/README.md`, section 7.

Strength labels as in the top `README.md`: **Measured**, **Measured (vendor)**, **Practice**, **Vendor claim**
(a seller's number with no sample or method), **Untraced**.

The brief was "not more, what is needed and well used". The verdict follows it: almost everything read
confirms what the pack already does. Four small changes were tested blind; three are in the pack (section 4).
Everything else is filed here, so nobody imports it later by mistake.

## 1. Pierre Herubel: who he is and what he is good for

B2B content creator (about 125K to 150K LinkedIn followers depending on the source), newsletter "Pierre's
Content Guides" on Substack, agency Contentpath. He writes about content and authority-led selling. He says
himself that outbound is not his specialty (Flowla interview). Nothing he publishes is a controlled
measurement: it is his own practice and his agency's results. His one dedicated outreach guide ("The LinkedIn
Social Selling Workflow", September 2024) is paywalled and was not read, so none of its steps are recorded.

What bears on prospecting falls in six ideas, all **Practice**:

1. **Warm, signal-led outbound.** The people who engaged with your content (a comment, a profile visit, a
   download) are the list, ahead of a cold Sales Navigator search. Engaged signals (contact with you or your
   content) rank above external ones (a hire, a funding round); leading with an external event alone can read
   as spam ("I saw you hired 3 SDRs so you must be interested"). Repeated engagement on one topic beats one
   random like.
2. **The signal gives the angle, the client type gives the framing.** Talk about the topic they engaged with,
   not about the fact that they engaged; a small firm and a large one are not offered the same thing.
3. **Directness follows the signal's strength.** A strong, specific signal (a download, a pricing page visit)
   gets a direct message naming it and one next step; a weak one (a like) gets a softer touch first.
4. **Ask permission before sending an asset.** "Do you want me to send it over?" rather than pushing a case
   study or a call. Pushing reads as needy.
5. **One front-end offer.** Several offers cause "positioning dilution and decision paralysis"; sell the bigger
   work after the first.
6. **Specific follow-ups, fast.** Never "just checking in": reuse the trigger that made them interested or bring
   something new (a case, a client figure, a resource). Answer an interested reply within the hour. After a
   sales call, follow up within 2 days. Someone not ready goes on a "to nurture" list touched every one to two
   weeks.

Also in his work, and left out on purpose: his content mix (about 70% expertise, 15% narrative, 10 to 15% offer
posts), profile advice (headline formula, banner, Featured offer), an engagement routine around one's own posts,
CPF (Claim, Proof, Filter, from a podcast summary), and "don't let AI write your copy". The pack writes outreach,
not posts; the voice skill already matches the user's own messages.

### What the pack took from him, and what it did not

| Idea | Verdict | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Engagers of a post are a warm list | Already in the pack | `bereach_find_posts` then `bereach_collect_engagers` (outreach-frameworks section 16) |
| The topic is the angle, not the like | Tested (C4), reverted | A comment on the user's own post first, and for someone else's post the topic as the premise: lost the re-test with isolated writers |
| Ask permission before sending | Already in the pack | "Shall I send you [the offer]?" in follow-ups; offers only the user really makes |
| One front-end offer | Already in the pack | ONE offer the user really made; never an invented audit |
| No "just checking in" | Already in the pack | Follow-up 1 brings something new or a real peer |
| Directness by signal strength | Rejected | A blind test had premise plus offer winning for every persona at every awareness level; a no-offer branch brings back the weaker arm |
| Nurture list every one to two weeks | Rejected | His context is after a sales call; it clashes with the stop after follow-up 2. Only the dated door was kept (C2) |
| Follow up within 2 days | Rejected | After a call, not for a cold person who never answered; the pack's 3 to 4, then 5 to 7 days stays |
| Reply to an interested answer fast | Already close | Interested replies sit on top of the daily Follow-ups block |
| CPF "Filter" clause | Rejected | The who-writes clause ("what I do for people like them") already does it |
| A 2-day window for engagers of a fresh post | Not tested | Plausible, nobody measured it; a candidate for a later test, not a rule |

## 2. Newsletters: vendors and practitioners

Senders: Gojiberry (7 emails), HeyReach, Scalezia with La
Growth Machine, Formula Agents, MimikFlow, Sendpilot, Lasse and Harald. Searches for Josh Braun, 30MPC,
Lavender, Jason Bay, Becc Holland, Will Allred, Justin Michael, Florin Tatulea, lemlist and Waalaxy found
nothing in these newsletters.

What is worth keeping:

- **Engagers convert better than other sources (Measured, vendor).** MimikFlow, 32 accounts, same period:
  inviting people who just reacted to posts on the user's topic gave 58% acceptance and 47% replies, against 31%
  and 21% from their other sources. Selection not controlled.
- **Competitors' and peers' audiences (Practice, vendor).** Gojiberry: pick five competitors, three of their
  employees who post, and keep the ICP matches among the engagers. "Who fits my ICP AND has a reason to care
  right now?" Lead tiers: warm inbound, referrals, real-time signals, then bought lists.
- **The note (Measured, vendor, no sample).** Gojiberry: no note gives about 2x acceptances; a note gives about
  1.5x more conversations among the accepted. Agrees with the pack's "a note is a filter".
- **Dormant pools (Measured, vendor, two accounts).** Formula Agents: old threads that went quiet and first
  degree connections never written to; 770 contacted, about 1 in 5 replied.
- **3Qs list filter (Practice, vendor).** HeyReach: why now, why them, why you; segment the list so each segment
  gets its own copy; measure reply, positive, meetings by segment. The method already does this in substance.
- **Buying-group roles (Practice, vendor).** HeyReach ABM: champion, decision maker, blocker, end user, each
  spoken to differently. The personas folder covers it.

What is not: Gojiberry's "15% to 45% with personalisation", "Tuesday is best", "60 to 80% of replies come after a
follow-up"; Formula Agents' "x100 replies within 5 minutes"; Sendpilot's "60% acceptance with 0 followers". No
sample, no method. Voice notes (Scalezia, "25%+ replies") are out: the tools do not send them.

## 3. The recognised experts and data checked

| Who | What holds | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| Rob Fitzpatrick, *The Mom Test* (2013) | A compliment, a generic claim or a future promise ("send me info", "maybe later") costs nothing and is not a yes; only commitment or a real next step counts | Taken (C2): a deferral is never counted as interested |
| Prospectio test 9 (randomized, 7,340) | Naming a shared colleague raised replies from 27.0% to 35.1% | Backs C1: a referral named by the lead is a real tie |
| Russell, Karpinska and Iyyer 2025 (ACL) | People who often use LLMs spot AI text at 92.7% with about 3 to 4% false positives; nonexperts sit at chance | Taken (C3): a counted check for AI tells after drafting |
| Yeomans et al. 2020 (OBHDP) | Acknowledging the other view in its own terms makes a written disagreement more persuasive | Measured backing for the existing "answer in their own words" reply rule |
| Chris Voss (labels, accusation audit) | Practice; the fMRI study cited for labels tested self-labelling of faces, not text | Rejected as a rule |
| Cialdini, *Pre-Suasion* (priming, Unity) | One small study, primary untraced; no effect data for Unity | Rejected |
| Lavender (28.3M emails, republished by LinkedIn) | 25 to 50 words +65% replies; 5th grade reading level +50% | Logged; no word or grade target (it would fight style matching) |
| Gong Labs, January 2026 | C-level 30.2% less likely to reply; Sales.co claims the opposite | Logged as a conflict |
| Gong with Jason Bay, 2025 | Pitching cuts replies up to 57% | Same data family as the 85M report, not independent |
| LinkedIn Sales Solutions | "Shared connection +78% response" | Vendor claim, footnote untraced |
| April Dunford, *Sales Pitch* (2023) | Insight, alternatives, perfect world, product, proof, ask | A meeting order; only the insight step fits a DM, and the premise line is it |
| Sam Nelson, Agoge Sequence | About 6 to 15 goal-tagged touches across email, call, LinkedIn | Exists (correction); not taken |
| Florin Tatulea, Kyle Coleman | One CEO-reply anecdote each, premise first | Citations only |
| Morgan Ingram, Daniel Disney, Jake Dunlap | Comment and help first, no pitch | Confirmed or contradicted by larger data (passive warm-up does not help) |
| Jed Mahrle | Paywalled | Unread |

## 4. What went into the pack (round 2)

All four won a first blind test (three judges, scores in `../method/README.md` section 7).
A re-test with isolated writers kept C1 to C3 and reverted C4:

- **C1. "Not me, ask X".** One line of thanks to the lead; the named colleague gets a brief and a first message
  whose line 1 is the referral in the lead's own words. Nobody else at the firm. (`linkedin-messages`, hard rule
  2 and follow-ups Replies.)
- **C2. A deferral is not a yes.** "Send me info" gets one question on what they want it for, or the offer if
  the first message named one; "not now" gets thanks and a question on when, saved as a `back:YYYY-MM` tag; no
  nurture sequence. Counted as answered, never interested. (`linkedin-messages` follow-ups, `measuring.md`.)
- **C3. AI tells counted after drafting.** No "not X but Y", no list of three, and in English none of a short
  word list, unless the user's own samples do it. (`linkedin-voice` Step 5.)
- **C4, reverted. A comment on the user's own post comes first.** For a lead found on someone else's post, the
  post's topic is the premise, never the reaction or whose post it was. It lost the re-test (5.5 against 7.7 without it), so
  `linkedin-messages` Step 3 and `first-dm.md` keep the old fact order.

## 5. Open

- A 2-day window for engagers of a fresh post against older posts: test on one account before any rule.
- Dormant threads (`bereach_inbox`) and first-degree connections never written to (`bereach_connections`) as a
  source before searching new people: measure on one account first.
- The C3 word list is English only; a French list needs its own measurement.
